messages.subject: Mutating across multiple dimensions
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to do calculations across at least two ordered dimensions, but the calculations should only use observations that have been specified. For example, if I have a j x k matrix, I want to take the product for all elements for j <= jj and k <= kk. That is, the product of everything to the left and up from the j, k element. But I might also want to take products for elements with j - 1 <= j <= j + 1 and k <= kk. That is, the product of elements within 1 row up and down and to the left of the j, k element.

With a matrix or array this may be straightforward, but I have data.frame with index variables j and k.

The following code does what I want, but it is terribly clunky. I'd rather not have to deal with keeping track of an elements position, as the formula jj + (n + (kk -1)) in the code only works because the indices in this case start from 1. I'd also like to easily express the filter as  a function argument.  

dt <- data.frame(j = rep(1:3, 3),
           k = sort(rep(1:3, 3)),
           y = runif(9))

compute_prods <- function(data)
{
  n <- max(data$j)
  out <- data

  for(kk in min(data$k):max(data$k) ){
    for(jj in min(data$j):max(data$j) ){
      pos  <- (jj)  + n * (kk - 1)
      these_rows <- filter_(out, paste0('j <=', jj, '&', 'k <=', kk))

      out[pos, 'val'] <- prod(these_rows[ , 'y'], na.rm = T)
    }
  }
  rm(jj, kk, pos)
  return(out)
}

compute_prods(dt)

I looked at the tbl_cube options, but I don't think that will work without a mutate function, since I'm not collapsing the data. Another option might be to recast the data frame into matrix and then apply over both dimensions then reshape back to data frame. Also, the data in the example does not have other dimensions, but in reality I need to perform this operation within other dimensions (e.g. j and k will be nested within an ID variable).

Any ideas from the group are appreciated.

-Bradley
